author: Natalie St. Denis
title: Albany Pine Bush to celebrate wildflower at annual festival - NewsBreak
text:
By Natalie St. Denis ,
1 hours ago
The video above features previous NEWS10 coverage of Karner blue butterflies being released at the Albany Pine Bush Preserve.
ALBANY, N.Y. ( NEWS10 ) — The Albany Pine Bush Preserve will host Lupine Fest again this year. The festival will highlight the wild blue lupine flower with daily programs throughout the month of May.
Download our WTEN+ streaming app on Roku, Fire TV and Apple TV! Wild blue lupine supports a diverse ecosystem, including two rare insects in the Pine Bush. Larvae of the federally endangered Karner blue butterfly feed exclusively on wild blue lupine leaves, and the state threatened frosted elfin butterfly feeds on its seed pods.
Visitors can expect guided hikes, science programs and lectures, nature journaling, interactive exhibits and more hands-on activities. Events including bird banding demonstrations, a fishing clinic and an evening of live music and local food vendors, deemed “Nature Night Out” are also in store.
Lineup and schedule announced for Albany’s 78th annual Tulip Festival “Lupine Fest is a celebration of everything that makes the Albany Pine Bush so special,” said Executive Director Christopher Hawver. “It’s an opportunity for people to connect with nature, learn something new, and be part of a community that values and protects this rare landscape.”
Passport Adventure is a popular highlight of Lupine Fest, which encourages participants to attend events and explore the Preserve and the Discovery Center through self-guided activities. Visitors can collect stamps for each activity they complete and earn small prizes along the way. Guests can also participate in real conservation efforts and shop locally crafted items at the Discovery Center gift shop.
Get the latest news, weather, sports and entertainment delivered right to your inbox! Lupine Fest is free for all ages to attend, but some programs require registration in advance. Visit the Albany Pine Bush Discovery Center located at 195 New Karner Road in Albany, to pick up a passport. View the full schedule and register for events online .
